title: Top VC Firms in India in 2026: Stages, Funds and How to Pitch
excerpt: The most active VC firms in India in 2026, ranked from Inc42 deal data, with each firm's stage, sectors, latest fund size and how founders should pitch them.
content:
The most active venture capital (VC) firms backing Indian startups in 2026 are Accel, Peak XV Partners and 3one4 Capital by deal count, with Zerodha's Rainmatter, Z47, Antler and IvyCap Ventures close behind, according to Inc42's quarterly investor rankings. The firms with the most new money to deploy include Peak XV, Accel, Nexus and Elevation, all of which raised or announced India funds between December 2025 and September 2026.

This guide explains how we built the list, what each firm backs and at which stage, the size of its latest fund, its named 2026 deals, and how founders should approach them. It was updated on 15 October 2026, ten days after Inc42 published its Q3 2026 ranking.

Key takeaways

  • Inc42 ranked Peak XV (16 deals) and Accel (13) as the most active equity VC firms in Q1 2026; Accel made 21 deals in the first half of the year.
  • 3one4 Capital was the most active early-stage equity VC in Q3 2026 with 19 deals, according to Inc42.
  • Fresh funds dated 2026 include Peak XV's $1.3 billion across three funds, Accel's $550 million India fund and Elevation's $500 million ninth India fund.
  • Money is flowing to fewer companies: Tracxn data reported by Outlook Business shows Indian tech firms raised $10.3 billion in January to September 2026, across far fewer rounds than a year earlier.
  • Most of these firms write their first cheques at seed or Series A, so the pitch has to prove a sharp problem, a credible team and a reason the timing is right.

How we built this list

We started with deal counts, not reputation. Inc42 publishes a ranking of the most active startup investors every quarter, based on its Indian Tech Startup Funding Report and its deal database. We used three editions: Q1 2026 (published 4 April 2026), H1 2026 (4 July 2026) and Q3 2026 (5 October 2026).

Those rankings mix venture debt lenders (Stride Ventures, Alteria Capital, BlackSoil, InnoVen Capital), angel networks and accelerators with equity VCs. Stride Ventures topped the overall table in all three editions, with 38 deals in Q1, 61 in H1 and 38 in Q3, according to Inc42. Because debt is a different product from equity, we removed lenders, angel networks and accelerator programmes and kept equity VC firms only.

Deal counts reward firms that write many small cheques, so we added a second test: the size and date of each firm's most recent dedicated India fund, taken from the firm's own announcement or from reputable outlets such as TechCrunch, Entrackr, YourStory and DealStreetAsia. Firms below are grouped accordingly. Where we could not find a dated, sourced figure, we say so rather than guess. Deal names come from the rankings or the firms' own posts; Inc42 did not publish round sizes for most of them.

The market in 2026: more money, fewer deals

Indian tech companies raised $10.3 billion between January and September 2026, about 7% more than a year earlier, according to Outlook Business's report on Tracxn data. The number of rounds fell sharply over the same period, which means capital is concentrating in fewer companies.

Inc42's quarterly figures tell the same story. Startups raised $2.3 billion across 271 deals in Q1 2026, 26% less than a year before, and Inc42 noted that the quarter had no round of $100 million or more. In Q3 2026 funding rose 5% to $2.2 billion, while the deal count fell 13% to 210. For founders, that means firms are still writing cheques but are pickier. You can follow individual rounds on our funding tracker.

The most active VC firms by 2026 deal count

1. Accel

Sectors: AI, consumer internet, fintech and advanced manufacturing, according to TechCrunch. Latest fund: a $550 million India fund, reported on 11 August 2026 as oversubscribed and closed within weeks. TechCrunch said Accel expects to start investing from it in 2027 and will keep using its earlier $650 million India fund (announced in 2022) until then.

2026 activity: 13 deals in Q1 and 21 in H1 2026, according to Inc42. Named portfolio companies in those rankings include Bounce, Dognosis and EtherealX (Q1), plus Rapido, FirstClub and Swish (H1).

2. Peak XV Partners

Stage: seed through growth. Sectors: mainly AI, fintech and consumer. Latest funds: $1.3 billion across an India seed fund, an India venture fund and an Asia-Pacific fund, announced in February 2026, according to Entrepreneur. These are the firm's first funds since it separated from Sequoia Capital in 2023.

2026 activity: Peak XV was the most active equity VC firm in Q1 2026 with 16 deals, according to Inc42, which named Agrani Labs, BambooBox and C2i Semiconductors among them.

3. 3one4 Capital

Stage: seed and Series A. Sectors: AI and SaaS, enterprise and manufacturing automation, fintech, deeptech and consumer internet. Latest fund: Fund IV closed at $200 million in May 2023, according to Business Standard. On 11 May 2026, Inc42 reported that Fund V is in the works with a likely target of $225 million and a proposed $20 million commitment from the IFC, the World Bank's private-sector arm. Inc42 said Fund IV's average cheques were $0.5 million to $5 million.

2026 activity: 11 deals in Q1 and 19 in Q3, the most of any equity VC that quarter, according to Inc42. Named companies include Elixiir Foods, Smalle and Unbox Robotics.

4. Rainmatter (Zerodha)

Sectors: climate, health and fintech-adjacent businesses, judging by the companies Inc42 lists. Rainmatter is the investment arm of the brokerage Zerodha, so it is a corporate investor rather than a fund with outside limited partners (LPs); we could not find a published fund size.

2026 activity: 39 deals in H1 2026, third overall, and 16 in Q3, according to Inc42. Named companies include Karo Sambhav, Polycycl, GreenWorms, SolarSquare and GalaxEye.

5. Z47 (formerly Matrix Partners India)

Sectors: fintech and consumer feature heavily among its named 2026 deals. Latest fund: we could not confirm a dated figure for a new fund from a primary source, so we have left it out.

2026 activity: six deals in Q1 2026, according to Inc42, which named Stable Money and The Whole Truth.

Other equity investors that made Inc42's 2026 top lists include Antler (14 deals in Q3), IvyCap Ventures (15 in Q3, including BatX Energies and BotSync), A Junior VC (13 in Q3) and Finvolve (19 in H1). If you are pre-seed, these smaller-cheque investors are often a better first call than the large funds.

Large VC firms with fresh India funds

6. Elevation Capital

Stage: seed and Series A as the core, according to the firm's own fund announcement. Sectors: the firm lists consumer tech, consumer brands, fintech and financial services, enterprise AI, frontier tech and healthcare. Latest fund: $500 million for its ninth India-focused fund, reported by DealStreetAsia on 14 July 2026. Its previous fund, Fund VIII, was $670 million (April 2022).

7. Nexus Venture Partners

Stage: inception, seed and Series A, with cheques often starting at a few hundred thousand dollars or around $1 million. Sectors in India: consumer, fintech, logistics and digital infrastructure. Latest fund: a $700 million eighth fund, about half of it reserved for India, according to TechCrunch (4 December 2025). TechCrunch reported that Nexus manages $3.2 billion and has backed more than 130 companies.

8. Lightspeed India

Stage: early stage. Sectors: AI companies across India and Southeast Asia. Latest fund: Lightspeed India Partners V is targeting $250 million and has about 80% of that committed, according to an investor letter reported by TechCrunch on 24 September 2026. That is half the size of its $500 million 2022 fund. The firm planned to start investing from it within two months.

9. Blume Ventures

Stage: seed and Series A, with starting cheques of $1.5 million to $5 million. Sectors: consumer, fintech, healthtech and deeptech. Latest fund: an initial close of Fund V at $175 million, with a final close target of $250–275 million by early 2026, according to Blume's own announcement (October 2025). Blume said the fund would back 30–35 startups and named early investments including Mave Health, Confido Health, Lucira, Ozi and PowerUp Money. We did not find a confirmed final close.

10. Chiratae Ventures

Stage: seed, Series A and Series B. Sectors: AI, deeptech, healthtech, consumer tech, fintech, SaaS, climate and spacetech, with an expansion into defence tech and quantum. Latest fund: a second close of Fund V at $150 million on 23 September 2025, with a final close expected by the first quarter of 2026, according to Chiratae. Early Fund V investments include HouseEazy, Pepsales, Mili and Zilo.

11. Stellaris Venture Partners

Stage: seed and Series A. Latest fund: Fund III closed at $300 million in November 2024, taking its assets under management above $600 million, according to YourStory. Stellaris said it would back 25–30 startups over three years. Its earlier portfolio includes Mamaearth, Zouk and Whatfix.

12. Prime Venture Partners

Stage: early stage, with initial cheques of $2.5 million to $3 million. Sectors: fintech and AI, among others. Latest fund: Fund V closed at $100 million in March 2025, according to Entrackr, and is meant to back 16–18 startups. Its smaller portfolio means each company gets more partner time, which matters for first-time founders.

Also worth knowing: Kalaari Capital. Kalaari backs early-stage companies and wrote in an April 2026 post that its portfolio company Digantara, a space-surveillance startup, had raised a $50 million Series B. We could not find a dated figure for a new Kalaari fund.

How to approach a VC firm in India

Start with fit. Every firm above publishes its stage and sector focus, and most state a typical first cheque: Blume starts at $1.5 million to $5 million, Prime at $2.5 million to $3 million, and Nexus often from a few hundred thousand dollars. Pitching a Series B growth story to a seed fund, or a hardware company to a consumer-only partner, wastes a meeting on both sides. Check the firm's recent deals on its site or on our startup news page to see who leads which sector.

Next, get the deck right. Sequoia Capital's widely used guide to writing a business plan lists ten parts: company purpose in one sentence, the problem, the solution, why now, market potential, competition, business model, team, financials and vision. Indian VCs reading hundreds of decks a quarter look for the first four quickly, so put them on the first few slides.

A practical sequence

  • Shortlist 15–25 firms whose stage, cheque size and sector match your round, using their fund announcements and recent deals.
  • Find the right partner, not the generic inbox. Most firms list partners by sector on their websites.
  • Ask for a warm introduction from a founder in that partner's portfolio, an angel investor or an accelerator. Accelerator programmes help here: Google's startup accelerator counted 20 deals in Inc42's Q3 2026 list.
  • Send a short email with the one-line company purpose, two or three traction numbers you can verify, the round size and a deck link.
  • Run the process in a tight window so that interest from one firm can inform others, and keep a data room ready for diligence.

Showcasing a product publicly helps too. Founders can list a launch on our launches page, which investors and early users browse.

Bottom line

India's most active equity VCs in 2026 are Accel, Peak XV and 3one4 Capital, while Elevation, Nexus, Lightspeed and Accel have the newest large pools of capital. With total funding up but deal counts down, according to Tracxn and Inc42 data, the firms are concentrating on fewer, stronger companies. Founders who pick firms by stage and sector, reach the right partner through a warm introduction and lead with a crisp problem and "why now" give themselves the best chance. This article is for information only; confirm terms with a qualified legal or financial adviser before signing a term sheet.

FAQ

Which is the most active VC firm in India in 2026?

Among equity VC firms, Peak XV led Inc42's Q1 2026 ranking with 16 deals, Accel made 21 deals in H1, and 3one4 Capital led in Q3 with 19. Venture debt firm Stride Ventures made more deals overall, but it lends rather than buys equity.

Which Indian VC firms invest at seed stage?

Peak XV (through its new India seed fund), Blume, 3one4, Elevation, Nexus, Stellaris and Chiratae all list seed among their core stages. Antler and A Junior VC were among the most active early-stage names in Q3 2026.

How much do Indian VCs invest in a first round?

It varies by firm. Blume says its starting cheques are $1.5 million to $5 million, Prime's are $2.5 million to $3 million, and Nexus often starts at a few hundred thousand dollars to about $1 million.

Do I need a warm introduction to pitch an Indian VC?

It is not required, and many firms accept submissions on their websites, but introductions from portfolio founders or angels usually get faster attention.

What should a pitch deck include?

Sequoia's guide lists company purpose, problem, solution, why now, market, competition, business model, team, financials and vision.
